decisions.choice: all Israel: the whole people, north and south together
decisions.reason: After the struggle for the throne in chapters 1-2 and the gift of wisdom in chapter 3, the writer states that Solomon's rule now reached the whole nation. The lists that follow show how that rule was organized: the officials of his court (verses 2-6) and the governors of the districts (verses 7-19).

decisions.choice: ruled as king (Balanced); was now king (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "was king ... king". Balanced uses "ruled" to avoid the repetition. Readable adds "now" to mark the settled state after the events of chapters 1-3, and says "the whole nation" for "all Israel".

pt.L: E estes [eram] os príncipes que [eram] dele: Azarias, filho de Zadoque, o sacerdote;
pt.B: Estes eram os seus altos oficiais: Azarias, filho de Zadoque, era o sacerdote;
pt.R: Estes eram os líderes do governo de Salomão: Azarias, filho de Zadoque, era o sacerdote.

decisions.choice: the officials: the chief men of the king's court
decisions.reason: The word can name princes, commanders or officials. Here it introduces the men who held the main offices of Solomon's court, as similar lists do for David (2 Samuel 8:16-18; 20:23-26).

decisions.choice: son of Zadok: a descendant, probably his grandson
decisions.reason: The priestly line in 1 Chronicles 5:34-35 runs Zadok, Ahimaaz, Azariah, so this Azariah may be Zadok's grandson. "Son" in Hebrew can name any male descendant.

decisions.choice: the priest: Azariah's office
alternatives: Azariah, son of Zadok the priest
decisions.reason: In this list each name is followed by the man's office, so "the priest" most likely belongs to Azariah. It could also describe Zadok ("son of Zadok the priest"), who is named as a priest in verse 4.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); high officials (Balanced); leaders of Solomon's government (Readable)
decisions.reason: This follows the usual wording for this word (Literal "princes", Balanced "officials", Readable "leaders"). Balanced adds "high" and Readable adds "of Solomon's government" because these are the king's chief ministers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: the list in verses 2-6 punctuated as one list
decisions.reason: The officials run on from verse 2 to verse 6, so Literal and Balanced end this verse with a semicolon. Readable uses full sentences.

decisions.choice: "príncipes" (L); "altos funcionarios" (B); "líderes del gobierno" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): the Hebrew sarim are the chief men of the court; Literal keeps the old word "príncipes", Balanced and Readable say what they were. Balanced and Literal punctuate verses 2-6 as one list (r-en-2).

decisions.choice: les princes (L); ses hauts fonctionnaires (B); les dirigeants du gouvernement (R)
decisions.reason: *Sarim* is "princes" at Literal, as in the French Samuel; Balanced and Readable name them as the king's chief officials, as the English does.

decisions.choice: wakuu (Literal); maafisa wakuu (Balanced); viongozi wa serikali (Readable)
decisions.reason: The *sarim* of Solomon's court: Literal "wakuu" (chiefs, princes), Balanced "maafisa wakuu" (high officials), Readable "viongozi wa serikali" (leaders of the government), following the English levels.

decisions.choice: "các quan trưởng" (L); "các quan đại thần" (B); "những người lãnh đạo trong triều đình" (R)
decisions.reason: The *sarim* are the chief men of the court (meaning decision), not princes of the royal family, which the Vietnamese "hoàng tử" would mean.

decisions.choice: "고관들" (L); "고위 관리들" (B); "나라를 다스리는 지도자들" (R)
decisions.reason: The *sarim* here are the king's chief officers of state; the older word 방백 is not current Korean.

decisions.choice: os príncipes (L); os seus altos oficiais (B); os líderes do governo de Salomão (R); Azarias
decisions.reason: The list of Solomon's officials (verses 2-6) follows the Portuguese of David's lists in 2 Samuel 8:15-18 and 20:23-26 office by office, so that the reader can see who kept his post: "[estava] sobre" (L), "era o comandante", "o encarregado" (B), "chefiava" (R), and the names Zadoque, Josafá filho de Ailude, Benaia filho de Joiada, Abiatar. The heading word follows the English per level. "Azarias" is the usual Brazilian form of the name.

en.R: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were the royal secretaries. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the official records.

ko.L: 시사의 아들 엘리호렙과 아히야는 서기관들, 아힐룻의 아들 여호사밧은 사관,
ko.B: 시사의 아들 엘리호렙과 아히야는 서기관이었으며, 아힐룻의 아들 여호사밧은 사관이었고,
ko.R: 시사의 아들 엘리호렙과 아히야는 왕의 서기관이었다. 아힐룻의 아들 여호사밧은 나라의 공식 기록을 맡았다.

pt.L: Eliorefe e Aías, filhos de Sisa, [eram] escrivães; Josafá, filho de Ailude, [era] cronista;
pt.B: Eliorefe e Aías, filhos de Sisa, serviam como secretários; Josafá, filho de Ailude, era o arquivista do reino;
pt.R: Eliorefe e Aías, filhos de Sisa, eram os secretários do rei. Josafá, filho de Ailude, cuidava dos registros oficiais do rei.

decisions.choice: secretaries and recorder: senior royal officials
decisions.reason: The secretary wrote the king's letters and records of state. The recorder (literally "one who causes to remember") kept the official records and may also have made the king's decisions known. Both offices appear among David's officials (2 Samuel 8:16-17) and Hezekiah's (Isaiah 36:3).

decisions.choice: Shisha: probably David's secretary under another form of his name
decisions.reason: David's secretary is called Seraiah (2 Samuel 8:17), Sheva (2 Samuel 20:25) and Shavsha (1 Chronicles 18:16). Shisha is very likely the same man, so his sons took over their father's office.

decisions.choice: Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the post he had under David
decisions.reason: He was David's recorder too (2 Samuel 8:16; 20:24). Solomon kept some of his father's officials and replaced others (2:35).

decisions.choice: scribes (Literal); secretaries (Balanced, Readable); kept the official records (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for these officials means "one who writes", which Literal keeps as "scribes"; Balanced and Readable name the office. Readable says what the recorder did, as in Isaiah 36:3.

decisions.choice: "escribas" (L), "secretarios" (B, R); "el cronista" (L, B), "llevaba los registros oficiales" (R)
decisions.reason: The secretary and the recorder follow the Kings terms note ("el secretario", "el cronista"); Literal says "escribas" and Readable describes the recorder's work, as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: scribes (L), secrétaires (B, R); l'archiviste
decisions.reason: The terms note's "le secrétaire" and "l'archiviste" for the court offices; Literal keeps "scribes" for "those who write", and Readable says what the recorder did.

decisions.choice: waandishi (Literal); makatibu (Balanced, Readable); mwandishi wa kumbukumbu
decisions.reason: The secretary and the recorder as the terms note and the Swahili of 2 Samuel 8:16-17 name them; Literal keeps "waandishi" (writers, scribes) for the Hebrew "those who write".

decisions.choice: "thư ký"; "sử quan" (L, B); "lo ghi chép sử sách của triều đình" (R)
decisions.reason: The Kings terms note's words for the secretary and the recorder; Readable says what the recorder did, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "서기관"; "사관" (L, B)
decisions.reason: As the Kings and Chronicles terms note for the secretary and the recorder; Readable says what the recorder did.

decisions.choice: Eliorefe, Aías, Sisa; escrivães (L), secretários (B, R); cronista (L), arquivista do reino (B), cuidava dos registros oficiais do rei (R)
decisions.reason: The offices keep the Portuguese words of 2 Samuel 8:16-17 and 20:24-25 at each level. The names take their usual Brazilian forms; "Sisa" is kept as the Hebrew gives it, though he is probably the Seraías or Seva of 2 Samuel (m2).

ko.B: 여호야다의 아들 브나야는 군대 사령관이었고, 사독과 아비아달은 제사장이었으며,
ko.R: 여호야다의 아들 브나야는 군대 사령관이었다. 사독과 아비아달은 제사장이었다.

pt.B: Benaia, filho de Joiada, era o comandante do exército; Zadoque e Abiatar eram sacerdotes;
pt.R: Benaia, filho de Joiada, era o comandante do exército. Zadoque e Abiatar eram sacerdotes.

decisions.choice: Benaiah over the army: Joab's replacement
decisions.reason: Solomon put Benaiah over the army in place of Joab after Joab was put to death (2:34-35).

decisions.choice: Abiathar: listed though Solomon had removed him
decisions.reason: Solomon had sent Abiathar away to Anathoth and put Zadok in his place (2:26-27, 35). His name here may come from the start of the reign, or he may have kept the title of priest after losing his place.

decisions.choice: commander of the army (Balanced); the army commander (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "over the army", which Literal keeps. Balanced and Readable use the usual title for this office in these books.

source.text: וַעֲזַרְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־נָתָ֖ן עַל־הַנִּצָּבִ֑ים וְזָב֧וּד בֶּן־נָתָ֛ן כֹּהֵ֖ן רֵעֶ֥ה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

en.R: Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the governors of the districts. Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and the king's trusted adviser.

vi.L: A-xa-ria con trai Na-than [cai quản] các quan cai trị; Xa-bút con trai Na-than [làm] thầy tế lễ, bạn của vua;
vi.B: A-xa-ria con trai Na-than cai quản các quan cai trị địa phương; Xa-bút con trai Na-than làm thầy tế lễ và là bạn thân của vua;
vi.R: A-xa-ria con trai Na-than cai quản các quan cai trị các vùng. Xa-bút con trai Na-than làm thầy tế lễ và là cố vấn thân tín của vua.

ko.L: 그리고 나단의 아들 아사랴는 관장들을 [맡았고], 나단의 아들 사붓은 제사장이자 왕의 벗,
ko.B: 나단의 아들 아사랴는 지방 관장들을 관리했고, 나단의 아들 사붓은 제사장이자 왕의 벗이었으며,
ko.R: 나단의 아들 아사랴는 각 지방을 다스리는 관장들을 관리했다. 나단의 아들 사붓은 제사장이었고 왕이 믿고 의지하는 조언자였다.

pt.L: E Azarias, filho de Natã, [estava] sobre os governadores; e Zabude, filho de Natã, [era] sacerdote, [o] amigo do rei;
pt.B: Azarias, filho de Natã, era o encarregado dos governadores dos distritos; Zabude, filho de Natã, era sacerdote e amigo do rei;
pt.R: Azarias, filho de Natã, chefiava os governadores dos distritos. Zabude, filho de Natã, era sacerdote e conselheiro de confiança do rei.

decisions.choice: the overseers: the twelve district governors
decisions.reason: The same word names the twelve men listed in verses 7-19, so Azariah was the official over all of them.

decisions.choice: friend of the king: a court office, the king's personal adviser
decisions.reason: "The king's friend" was a title. Hushai held it under David (2 Samuel 15:37; 16:16) and gave him counsel at a time of danger.

decisions.choice: priest: here perhaps a high official at the king's side
decisions.reason: The word normally means a priest. David's sons are also called priests (2 Samuel 8:18), where 1 Chronicles 18:17 says "first at the king's side", so here it may name a senior royal post rather than service at the altar.

decisions.choice: Nathan: probably one man, father of both officials
decisions.reason: This may be Nathan the prophet, who supported Solomon (1:11-14), or David's son Nathan (2 Samuel 5:14). The text does not say.

decisions.choice: district governors (Balanced, Readable); trusted adviser (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "district" to show these are the governors of verse 7. Readable explains the title "the king's friend".

decisions.choice: "consejero de confianza del rey" (R)
decisions.reason: "Friend of the king" was a court office; Literal and Balanced keep "amigo del rey", Readable says what he did, as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: les intendants (L); les gouverneurs de district (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps a word for men set over supplies; Balanced and Readable say "gouverneurs de district", as the English adds "district", so that the twelve of verse 7 are recognised.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa wilaya
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable call the twelve governors of verse 7 "wakuu wa wilaya" (district heads); Literal keeps "wasimamizi" (overseers).

decisions.choice: "các quan cai trị" (L); "các quan cai trị địa phương" (B); "các quan cai trị các vùng" (R)
decisions.reason: The twelve men set over the districts (meaning decision); a plain descriptive title, kept for them through verses 7-19.

decisions.choice: "관장" for the twelve district governors
decisions.reason: One word for the *nitsavim* through the chapter; 총독 suggests a foreign empire's governor.

decisions.choice: os governadores (dos distritos); Zabude; amigo do rei (L, B), conselheiro de confiança do rei (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "governadores" for the twelve men over Solomon's districts (m1), the plain word for a man set over a region; "prefeito" would read as a town mayor in Brazil. "Amigo do rei" keeps the court title (m2), as Hushai's "amigo de Davi" in 2 Samuel; Readable explains it, as the English does.

source.text: וַאֲחִישָׁ֖ר עַל־הַבָּ֑יִת וַאֲדֹנִירָ֥ם בֶּן־עַבְדָּ֖א עַל־הַמַּֽס׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And Ahishar [was] over the house; and Adoniram son of Abda [was] over the forced labor.

en.L: And Ahishar [was] over the house; and Adoniram son of Abda [was] over the forced labor.
en.B: Ahishar was in charge of the palace, and Adoniram son of Abda had charge of the forced labor.
en.R: Ahishar managed the king's palace. Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the people who were forced to work for the king.

es.L: y Ahisar [estaba] sobre la casa; y Adoniram hijo de Abda [estaba] sobre el trabajo forzado.
es.B: Ahisar era el mayordomo del palacio, y Adoniram hijo de Abda estaba a cargo del trabajo forzado.
es.R: Ahisar administraba el palacio del rey. Adoniram hijo de Abda estaba a cargo de la gente obligada a trabajar para el rey.

fr.L: Et Ahishar [était] sur la maison ; et Adoniram fils d’Abda [était] sur la corvée.
fr.B: Ahishar était chef du palais, et Adoniram fils d’Abda était responsable de la corvée.
fr.R: Ahishar dirigeait le palais du roi. Adoniram, le fils d’Abda, était responsable des gens obligés de travailler pour le roi.

sw.L: Ahishari [alikuwa] juu ya nyumba; na Adoniramu mwana wa Abda [alikuwa] juu ya kazi ya kulazimishwa.
sw.B: Ahishari alikuwa msimamizi wa ikulu, na Adoniramu mwana wa Abda alikuwa msimamizi wa kazi ya kulazimishwa.
sw.R: Ahishari aliisimamia ikulu ya mfalme. Adoniramu mwana wa Abda aliwasimamia watu waliolazimishwa kumfanyia mfalme kazi.

vi.L: A-hi-sa [cai quản] cung điện; A-đô-ni-ram con trai Áp-đa [cai quản] việc lao dịch.
vi.B: A-hi-sa làm quan cai quản cung điện, còn A-đô-ni-ram con trai Áp-đa cai quản việc lao dịch.
vi.R: A-hi-sa quản lý cung điện của vua. A-đô-ni-ram con trai Áp-đa cai quản những người bị bắt làm công việc nặng nhọc cho vua.

ko.L: 그리고 아히살은 궁을 [맡았고], 압다의 아들 아도니람은 강제 노역을 [맡았다].
ko.B: 아히살은 궁내 대신이었고, 압다의 아들 아도니람은 강제 노역을 감독했다.
ko.R: 아히살은 왕궁의 일을 관리했다. 압다의 아들 아도니람은 왕을 위해 억지로 일해야 하는 사람들을 감독했다.

pt.L: E Aisar [estava] sobre a casa; e Adonirão, filho de Abda, [estava] sobre o trabalho forçado.
pt.B: Aisar era o encarregado do palácio, e Adonirão, filho de Abda, era o encarregado do trabalho forçado.
pt.R: Aisar administrava o palácio do rei. Adonirão, filho de Abda, chefiava os homens obrigados a trabalhar para o rei.

decisions.choice: over the house: chief steward of the royal palace
decisions.reason: The man "over the house" ran the king's household and estates and could speak for the king (Isaiah 22:15; 36:3; 2 Kings 15:5).

decisions.choice: the forced labor: work crews the king raised for his building
decisions.reason: The word names compulsory work for the state. Solomon's labor gangs built the temple, the palace and his fortified cities (5:27-28; 9:15-22). Adoniram, also called Adoram, held the post under David too (2 Samuel 20:24) and was still over it under Rehoboam (12:18); the burden of this labor helped split the kingdom (12:4, 18).

decisions.choice: in charge of the palace (Balanced); managed the king's palace; the people who were forced to work for the king (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "over the house", which Literal keeps. Balanced uses the same wording as Isaiah 36:3. Readable explains what forced labor was.

decisions.choice: "el mayordomo del palacio" (B)
decisions.reason: The officer "over the house" follows the Kings terms note for Spanish, "el mayordomo del palacio", at Balanced; Literal keeps "sobre la casa" and Readable describes the work (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: chef du palais; la corvée
alternatives: intendant du palais; le travail forcé
decisions.reason: "Le chef du palais" is the terms note's title for the officer "over the house"; "la corvée" names unpaid work owed to the king, which Readable explains.

decisions.choice: msimamizi wa ikulu
decisions.reason: "Over the house" is "msimamizi wa ikulu", the title the terms note settles for these books; Literal keeps the Hebrew "juu ya nyumba".

decisions.choice: "lao dịch" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The work crews raised by the king (meaning decision); "lao dịch" is the usual word for forced labor owed to a ruler, and Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: "궁내 대신"
decisions.reason: As the Kings and Chronicles terms note for the officer "over the house".

decisions.choice: Adonirão; o trabalho forçado (L, B); os homens obrigados a trabalhar para o rei (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 5:28; 12:18): "Adonirão" takes the nasal ending Portuguese writes for a final "-am", as the same man is "Adorão" in 2 Samuel 20:24 in Portuguese, and the office keeps the words of that verse at each level: "trabalho forçado" (m2), as Joshua 16:10 and Judges 1:28 in Portuguese, and Readable's explanation.

source.text: וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֞ה שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֤ר נִצָּבִים֙ עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְכִלְכְּל֥וּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְאֶת־בֵּית֑וֹ חֹ֧דֶשׁ בַּשָּׁנָ֛ה יִהְיֶ֥ה עַל־הָאֶחָ֖ד לְכַלְכֵּֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And to Solomon [were] twelve overseers over all Israel, and they supplied the king and his household; a month in the year was on the one to supply.

en.L: And Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel, and they provided for the king and his household; a month in the year it was [laid] on each one to provide.
en.B: Solomon had twelve district governors over all Israel, who supplied food for the king and his household. Each of them had to provide for one month in the year.
en.R: Solomon had twelve governors in charge of districts all over Israel. They supplied the food for the king and for everyone in his palace. Each governor had to provide the food for one month every year.

es.L: Y Salomón tenía doce gobernadores sobre todo Israel, y ellos abastecían al rey y a su casa; a cada uno le tocaba abastecer un mes al año.
es.B: Salomón tenía doce gobernadores de distrito sobre todo Israel, que abastecían de alimentos al rey y a su casa. Cada uno debía hacerlo durante un mes al año.
es.R: Salomón tenía doce gobernadores a cargo de distritos por todo Israel. Ellos daban la comida para el rey y para todos los de su palacio. Cada gobernador tenía que dar la comida durante un mes cada año.

fr.L: Et Salomon avait douze intendants sur tout Israël, et ils pourvoyaient [aux besoins du] roi et de sa maison ; un mois dans l’année, c’était à chacun de pourvoir.
fr.B: Salomon avait douze gouverneurs de district sur tout Israël, qui fournissaient les vivres du roi et de sa maison. Chacun d’eux devait y pourvoir un mois par an.
fr.R: Salomon avait douze gouverneurs responsables de districts dans tout Israël. Ils fournissaient la nourriture pour le roi et pour tous les gens de son palais. Chaque gouverneur devait fournir la nourriture pendant un mois chaque année.

sw.L: Na Sulemani alikuwa na wasimamizi kumi na wawili juu ya Israeli wote, nao walimpatia mfalme na nyumba yake mahitaji; mwezi mmoja katika mwaka ilikuwa [juu] ya kila mmoja kuwapatia.
sw.B: Sulemani alikuwa na wakuu wa wilaya kumi na wawili juu ya Israeli wote, waliompatia mfalme na watu wa nyumbani mwake chakula. Kila mmoja wao alipaswa kutoa mahitaji kwa mwezi mmoja katika mwaka.
sw.R: Sulemani alikuwa na wakuu kumi na wawili wa wilaya katika Israeli yote. Wao walileta chakula cha mfalme na cha watu wote wa ikulu yake. Kila mkuu wa wilaya alipaswa kuleta chakula kwa mwezi mmoja kila mwaka.

vi.L: Sa-lô-môn có mười hai quan cai trị trên cả Y-sơ-ra-ên, họ cung cấp cho vua và hoàng gia; mỗi người phải cung cấp một tháng trong năm.
vi.B: Sa-lô-môn có mười hai quan cai trị địa phương trên khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên, lo cung cấp lương thực cho vua và hoàng gia. Mỗi người phải cung cấp trong một tháng mỗi năm.
vi.R: Sa-lô-môn có mười hai quan cai trị các vùng trên khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên. Họ lo cung cấp lương thực cho vua và mọi người trong cung điện. Mỗi quan cai trị phải cung cấp lương thực trong một tháng mỗi năm.

ko.L: 그리고 솔로몬에게는 온 이스라엘을 맡은 관장 열두 명이 있었다. 그들은 왕과 그의 집안을 위해 [식량을] 공급했다. 각 사람이 일 년에 한 달씩 공급할 [책임이] 있었다.
ko.B: 솔로몬은 온 이스라엘에 지방 관장 열두 명을 두었다. 그들은 왕과 왕실에 필요한 식량을 공급했는데, 각 사람이 일 년에 한 달씩 책임을 맡았다.
ko.R: 솔로몬은 이스라엘 전국에 각 지방을 다스리는 관장 열두 명을 두었다. 그들은 왕과 왕궁에 사는 모든 사람에게 필요한 음식을 공급했다. 관장마다 일 년에 한 달씩 음식을 책임졌다.

pt.L: E Salomão tinha doze governadores sobre todo o Israel, e eles sustentavam o rei e a sua casa; um mês no ano cabia a cada um sustentar.
pt.B: Salomão tinha doze governadores de distrito sobre todo o Israel, que forneciam alimento para o rei e para a sua casa. Cada um deles tinha de prover o sustento durante um mês por ano.
pt.R: Salomão tinha doze governadores que cuidavam de distritos em todo o Israel. Eles forneciam a comida para o rei e para todas as pessoas do palácio. Cada governador tinha de fornecer a comida durante um mês por ano.

decisions.choice: supplied: provided food and goods for
decisions.reason: The verb means to sustain or feed, as Joseph fed his family in Egypt (Genesis 45:11; 47:12). The size of the daily supply is set out in 5:2-3 and 5:7-8.

decisions.choice: twelve districts: a new division of the land
decisions.reason: The districts in verses 8-19 do not simply follow the tribes. Some are named by tribe, others by towns and regions, so the old tribal lands were partly redrawn for the king's needs. Judah is not named in the list (see verse 19).

decisions.choice: each one: the written text and the traditional reading differ only by the word "the"
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text and the reading handed down with it differ by the article on "one". Either way the sense is "each one".

decisions.choice: supplied food (Balanced, Readable); everyone in his palace (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was supplied, as the following verses show. Readable explains "his household" as the people of the palace.

source.text: וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמוֹתָ֔ם בֶּן־ח֖וּר בְּהַ֥ר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And these [are] their names: Ben-hur, in [the] hill country of Ephraim.

en.L: And these [are] their names: Ben-hur, in [the] hill country of Ephraim;
en.B: These are their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
en.R: These are the names of the governors and their districts: Ben-hur (that is, the son of Hur) was over the hill country of Ephraim.

es.L: Y estos [son] sus nombres: Ben-hur, en la región montañosa de Efraín;
es.B: Estos son sus nombres: Ben-hur, en la región montañosa de Efraín;
es.R: Estos son los nombres de los gobernadores y sus distritos: Ben-hur (es decir, el hijo de Hur) estaba a cargo de la región montañosa de Efraín.

fr.L: Et voici leurs noms : Ben-Hour, dans la montagne d’Éphraïm ;
fr.B: Voici leurs noms : Ben-Hour, dans la montagne d’Éphraïm ;
fr.R: Voici les noms des gouverneurs et de leurs districts : Ben-Hour (c’est-à-dire le fils de Hour) était responsable de la région des montagnes d’Éphraïm.

sw.L: Na haya [ndiyo] majina yao: Ben-huri, katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu;
sw.B: Haya ndiyo majina yao: Ben-huri, katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu;
sw.R: Haya ndiyo majina ya wakuu wa wilaya na wilaya zao: Ben-huri (yaani, mwana wa Huri) alikuwa juu ya nchi ya milima ya Efraimu.

vi.L: Đây [là] tên của họ: Bên-Hu-rơ, tại vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im;
vi.B: Đây là tên của họ: Bên-Hu-rơ, tại vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im;
vi.R: Đây là tên các quan cai trị và vùng của họ: Bên-Hu-rơ (nghĩa là con trai Hu-rơ) cai trị vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im.

ko.L: 그리고 그들의 이름은 이러하다. 에브라임 산지에는 벤훌,
ko.B: 그들의 이름은 이러하다. 에브라임 산지에는 벤훌,
ko.R: 관장들의 이름과 그들이 맡은 지역은 이러하다. 벤훌(훌의 아들이라는 뜻)은 에브라임 산지를 맡았다.

pt.L: E estes [são] os seus nomes: Ben-Hur, na região montanhosa de Efraim;
pt.B: Estes são os seus nomes: Ben-Hur, na região montanhosa de Efraim;
pt.R: Estes são os nomes dos governadores e dos seus distritos: Ben-Hur (isto é, o filho de Hur) governava a região montanhosa de Efraim.

decisions.choice: Ben-hur: "son of Hur", a man known by his father's name
decisions.reason: Five of the governors are given only as "son of" someone (verses 8, 9, 10, 11 and 13). The list may come from a document whose first names were lost, or these men may simply have been known by their families. The name is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: the hill country of Ephraim: the central highlands
decisions.reason: This was the heart of the northern tribes, around Shechem and Bethel.

decisions.choice: Ben-hur, Ben-deker, Ben-hesed, Ben-abinadab, Ben-geber at every level
decisions.reason: These five governors keep the Hebrew form as one name, joined with a hyphen, in all three levels. Readable explains the meaning once, here.

decisions.choice: the governors and their districts; was over
decisions.reason: Readable says what the list gives and supplies "was over" for each governor's district, here and in verses 9-19.

decisions.choice: "Ben-hur", "Ben-decar", "Ben-hesed", "Ben-abinadab", "Ben-geber" at every level
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): these governors are known by their fathers' names, and Spanish keeps the Hebrew "Ben-" at every level; Readable explains the first one.

decisions.choice: Ben-Hour, Ben-Déqer, Ben-Hésed, Ben-Abinadab, Ben-Guéber
decisions.reason: The five governors known by their fathers' names keep one hyphenated name at every level, in French spelling (ou for u, q for qof, gu before e); Readable explains the meaning once, here.

decisions.choice: Ben-huri, Ben-dekeri, Ben-hesedi, Ben-abinadabu, Ben-geberi
decisions.reason: These five governors keep the Hebrew "Ben-" (son of) as part of one name at every level, as the English does; Readable explains it once here.

decisions.choice: "Bên-Hu-rơ", "Bên-Đê-ke", "Bên-Hê-sết", "Bên-A-bi-na-đáp", "Bên-Ghê-be"
decisions.reason: As the English, these men are known by their fathers' names; Vietnamese keeps them as names, with "Bên-" ("son of"), and Readable explains the first.

decisions.choice: "벤훌", "벤데겔", "벤헤셋", "벤아비나답", "벤게벨" as names
decisions.reason: As the English: the men are known by their fathers' names, kept as names at every level; Readable explains the first once.

decisions.choice: Ben-Hur, Ben-Dequer, Ben-Hesede, Ben-Abinadabe, Ben-Geber; governava (R)
decisions.reason: As the English, the five "son of" governors (m1) keep the Hebrew form as one name with a hyphen, the second part capitalised as in "Ben-Hadade", and Readable explains it once, here. Readable says "governava" for the English "was over" through verse 19. "A região montanhosa de Efraim" as Joshua and Judges in Portuguese.

vi.R: Bên-Đê-ke cai trị Ma-cát, Sa-an-bim, Bết-Sê-mết và Ê-lôn Bết-Ha-nan.

pt.R: Ben-Dequer governava Macaz, Saalbim, Bete-Semes e Elom-Bete-Hanã.

decisions.choice: the western foothills, once the land of Dan
decisions.reason: Shaalbim and Beth-shemesh lie in the low hills west of Jerusalem, in the area first given to Dan (Joshua 19:41-43; Judges 1:35). Ben-deker is a "son of" name, as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: Elon-beth-hanan: one place
decisions.reason: The words may name one town, Elon-beth-hanan, or two, Elon and Beth-hanan. No town of either name is known for certain.

decisions.choice: Macaz, Saalbim, Bete-Semes, Elom-Bete-Hanã
decisions.reason: "Saalbim" and "Bete-Semes" as Judges 1:35 and Joshua in Portuguese; the other names take the usual Brazilian spelling. Elom-Bete-Hanã is written as one place with hyphens, as the English reads it (m2).

records.literal_gloss: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth; to him [were] Socoh and all [the] land of Hepher.

en.L: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth; his [were] Socoh and all [the] land of Hepher;
en.B: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth; Socoh and all the land of Hepher were his;
en.R: Ben-hesed was over Arubboth. Socoh and the whole region of Hepher were also in his district.

es.L: Ben-hesed, en Arubot; suyos [eran] Soco y toda la tierra de Hefer;
es.B: Ben-hesed, en Arubot; Soco y toda la tierra de Hefer eran suyos;
es.R: Ben-hesed estaba a cargo de Arubot. Soco y toda la región de Hefer también estaban en su distrito.

fr.L: Ben-Hésed, à Aroubboth ; à lui [étaient] Soko et tout le pays de Hépher ;
fr.B: Ben-Hésed, à Aroubboth ; Soko et tout le pays de Hépher étaient à lui ;
fr.R: Ben-Hésed était responsable d’Aroubboth. Soko et toute la région de Hépher faisaient aussi partie de son district.

sw.L: Ben-hesedi, katika Arubothi; Soko na nchi yote ya Heferi [vilikuwa] vyake;
sw.B: Ben-hesedi, katika Arubothi; Soko na nchi yote ya Heferi vilikuwa chini yake;
sw.R: Ben-hesedi alikuwa juu ya Arubothi. Soko na eneo lote la Heferi pia vilikuwa katika wilaya yake.

vi.L: Bên-Hê-sết, tại A-ru-bốt; Sô-cô và cả xứ Hê-phe [thuộc về] ông;
vi.B: Bên-Hê-sết, tại A-ru-bốt; Sô-cô và cả xứ Hê-phe thuộc quyền ông;
vi.R: Bên-Hê-sết cai trị A-ru-bốt. Sô-cô và cả miền Hê-phe cũng thuộc vùng của ông.

ko.L: 아룹봇에는 벤헤셋, 그에게 소고와 헤벨 온 땅이 [속했다].
ko.B: 아룹봇에는 벤헤셋, 소고와 헤벨 온 땅도 그의 관할이었다.
ko.R: 벤헤셋은 아룹봇을 맡았다. 소고와 헤벨 지역 전체도 그가 맡은 지역에 들어 있었다.

pt.L: Ben-Hesede, em Arubote; dele [eram] Socó e toda a terra de Hefer;
pt.B: Ben-Hesede, em Arubote; Socó e toda a terra de Hefer eram dele;
pt.R: Ben-Hesede governava Arubote. Socó e toda a região de Hefer também faziam parte do seu distrito.

decisions.choice: to him: belonging to his district
decisions.reason: "To him" means these places were under his charge, as in verse 13.

decisions.choice: Socoh and the land of Hepher: in the coastal plain of Sharon
decisions.reason: This Socoh is probably not the Socoh of Judah (Joshua 15:35) but a town in the plain north of it. Hepher was a clan area of Manasseh (Joshua 12:17; 17:2). Ben-hesed is a "son of" name, as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: the whole region of Hepher
decisions.reason: Readable says "region" for "land", since a part of the country is meant.

source.text: בֶּן־אֲבִֽינָדָ֖ב כָּל־נָ֣פַת דֹּ֑אר טָפַת֙ בַּת־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה הָ֥יְתָה לּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Ben-abinadab, all [the] height of Dor; Taphath daughter of Solomon became to him as wife.

en.L: Ben-abinadab, all Naphath-dor; Taphath daughter of Solomon became his wife;
en.B: Ben-abinadab, all Naphath-dor (Taphath, Solomon's daughter, was his wife);
en.R: Ben-abinadab was over all the hills around Dor. He was married to Taphath, Solomon's daughter.

es.L: Ben-abinadab, toda Nafat-dor; Tafat hija de Salomón fue su esposa;
es.B: Ben-abinadab, en toda Nafat-dor (Tafat, hija de Salomón, era su esposa);
es.R: Ben-abinadab estaba a cargo de todas las colinas alrededor de Dor. Estaba casado con Tafat, hija de Salomón.

fr.L: Ben-Abinadab, tout Naphath-Dor ; Taphath fille de Salomon devint sa femme ;
fr.B: Ben-Abinadab, tout Naphath-Dor (Taphath, fille de Salomon, était sa femme) ;
fr.R: Ben-Abinadab était responsable de toutes les collines autour de Dor. Il avait épousé Taphath, la fille de Salomon.

sw.L: Ben-abinadabu, Nafath-dori yote; Tafathi binti Sulemani akawa mke wake;
sw.B: Ben-abinadabu, katika Nafath-dori yote (Tafathi, binti Sulemani, alikuwa mke wake);
sw.R: Ben-abinadabu alikuwa juu ya vilima vyote vinavyozunguka Dori. Alikuwa amemwoa Tafathi, binti Sulemani.

vi.L: Bên-A-bi-na-đáp, cả Na-phát Đô-rơ; Ta-phát con gái Sa-lô-môn làm vợ ông;
vi.B: Bên-A-bi-na-đáp, tại cả Na-phát Đô-rơ (Ta-phát, con gái Sa-lô-môn, là vợ ông);
vi.R: Bên-A-bi-na-đáp cai trị cả vùng đồi núi quanh Đô-rơ. Ông cưới Ta-phát, con gái Sa-lô-môn.

ko.L: 나밧돌 전체에는 벤아비나답, 솔로몬의 딸 다밧이 그의 아내가 되었다.
ko.B: 나밧돌 전 지역에는 벤아비나답(솔로몬의 딸 다밧이 그의 아내였다),
ko.R: 벤아비나답은 돌 주변의 모든 언덕 지역을 맡았다. 그는 솔로몬의 딸 다밧과 결혼했다.

pt.L: Ben-Abinadabe, toda Nafate-Dor; Tafate, filha de Salomão, tornou-se a sua mulher;
pt.B: Ben-Abinadabe, toda Nafate-Dor (Tafate, filha de Salomão, era a sua mulher);
pt.R: Ben-Abinadabe governava todas as colinas ao redor de Dor. Ele era casado com Tafate, filha de Salomão.

decisions.choice: Naphath-dor: the heights of Dor
decisions.reason: Dor was a port on the coast south of Mount Carmel. The first word means "height" or "ridge", the hills behind the town (Joshua 11:2; 12:23). Ben-abinadab is a "son of" name, as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: Solomon's daughter as a governor's wife
decisions.reason: Marriage tied this governor, and Ahimaaz in verse 15, to the royal family and so to the king's interests.

decisions.choice: all the hills around Dor
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name Naphath-dor, as Joshua 11:2 does.

source.text: בַּֽעֲנָא֙ בֶּן־אֲחִיל֔וּד תַּעְנַ֖ךְ וּמְגִדּ֑וֹ וְכָל־בֵּ֣ית שְׁאָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֵ֨צֶל צָרְתַ֜נָה מִתַּ֣חַת לְיִזְרְעֶ֗אל מִבֵּ֤ית שְׁאָן֙ עַ֚ד אָבֵ֣ל מְחוֹלָ֔ה עַ֖ד מֵעֵ֥בֶר לְיָקְמֳעָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Baana son of Ahilud, Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean, which [is] beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as [the] other side of Jokmeam.

en.L: Baana son of Ahilud: Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean, which [is] beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;
en.B: Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and on beyond Jokmeam;
en.R: Baana son of Ahilud was over Taanach and Megiddo and the whole area of Beth-shean. That area lay next to Zarethan, below the town of Jezreel, and reached from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and on past Jokmeam.

es.L: Baana hijo de Ahilud: Taanac y Meguido y todo Bet-sán, que [está] junto a Saretán, debajo de Jezreel, desde Bet-sán hasta Abel-mehola, hasta más allá de Jocmeam;
es.B: Baana hijo de Ahilud, en Taanac, Meguido y todo Bet-sán, junto a Saretán, debajo de Jezreel, desde Bet-sán hasta Abel-mehola y más allá de Jocmeam;
es.R: Baana hijo de Ahilud estaba a cargo de Taanac, Meguido y toda la zona de Bet-sán. Esa zona estaba junto a Saretán, más abajo del pueblo de Jezreel, y se extendía desde Bet-sán hasta Abel-mehola y más allá de Jocmeam.

fr.L: Baana fils d’Ahiloud : Taanak, et Meguiddo, et tout Beth-Shéan, qui [est] à côté de Tsarethân, au-dessous de Jizreël, depuis Beth-Shéan jusqu’à Abel-Mehola, jusqu’au-delà de Yoqméam ;
fr.B: Baana fils d’Ahiloud, à Taanak et Meguiddo, et dans tout Beth-Shéan, près de Tsarethân, au-dessous de Jizreël, depuis Beth-Shéan jusqu’à Abel-Mehola et au-delà de Yoqméam ;
fr.R: Baana, le fils d’Ahiloud, était responsable de Taanak, de Meguiddo et de toute la région de Beth-Shéan. Cette région se trouvait à côté de Tsarethân, au-dessous de la ville de Jizreël, et elle allait de Beth-Shéan jusqu’à Abel-Mehola et plus loin que Yoqméam.

sw.L: Baana mwana wa Ahiludi: Taanaki na Megido na Beth-sheani yote, [ulio] kando ya Sarethani chini ya Yezreeli, tangu Beth-sheani mpaka Abel-mehola, mpaka ng'ambo ya Yokmeamu;
sw.B: Baana mwana wa Ahiludi, katika Taanaki na Megido na Beth-sheani yote kando ya Sarethani chini ya Yezreeli, tangu Beth-sheani mpaka Abel-mehola na kupita Yokmeamu;
sw.R: Baana mwana wa Ahiludi alikuwa juu ya Taanaki na Megido na eneo lote la Beth-sheani. Eneo hilo lilikuwa kando ya Sarethani, chini ya mji wa Yezreeli, na lilienea tangu Beth-sheani mpaka Abel-mehola na kupita Yokmeamu.

vi.L: Ba-a-na con trai A-hi-lút: Tha-a-nác, Mê-ghi-đô và cả Bết-san, [là vùng] bên cạnh Xát-than, phía dưới Gít-rê-ên, từ Bết-san đến A-bên Mê-hô-la, cho đến bên kia Giốc-mê-am;
vi.B: Ba-a-na con trai A-hi-lút, tại Tha-a-nác, Mê-ghi-đô và cả Bết-san gần Xát-than phía dưới Gít-rê-ên, từ Bết-san đến A-bên Mê-hô-la và qua khỏi Giốc-mê-am;
vi.R: Ba-a-na con trai A-hi-lút cai trị Tha-a-nác, Mê-ghi-đô và cả vùng Bết-san. Vùng ấy nằm cạnh Xát-than, phía dưới thành Gít-rê-ên, trải dài từ Bết-san đến A-bên Mê-hô-la và qua khỏi Giốc-mê-am.

ko.L: 아힐룻의 아들 바아나는 다아낙과 므깃도와, 이스르엘 아래 사르단 곁에 [있는] 벧스안 전체, 곧 벧스안에서 아벨므홀라까지, 욕므암 건너편까지,
ko.B: 다아낙과 므깃도와, 이스르엘 아래 사르단 곁에 있는 벧스안 전 지역, 곧 벧스안에서 아벨므홀라를 지나 욕므암 너머까지는 아힐룻의 아들 바아나,
ko.R: 아힐룻의 아들 바아나는 다아낙과 므깃도와 벧스안 지역 전체를 맡았다. 그 지역은 이스르엘 성읍 아래 사르단 곁에 있었으며, 벧스안에서 아벨므홀라까지, 그리고 욕므암 너머까지 이르렀다.

pt.L: Baana, filho de Ailude: Taanaque, e Megido, e toda Bete-Seã, que [está] junto a Zaretã, abaixo de Jezreel, desde Bete-Seã até Abel-Meolá, até além de Jocmeão;
pt.B: Baana, filho de Ailude, em Taanaque e Megido e em toda Bete-Seã, junto a Zaretã, abaixo de Jezreel, desde Bete-Seã até Abel-Meolá e mais além de Jocmeão;
pt.R: Baana, filho de Ailude, governava Taanaque, Megido e toda a região de Bete-Seã. Essa região ficava perto de Zaretã, abaixo da cidade de Jezreel, e ia de Bete-Seã até Abel-Meolá e mais além de Jocmeão.

decisions.choice: the Jezreel valley and the Jordan valley near Beth-shean
decisions.reason: Taanach, Megiddo and Beth-shean were strong old cities that Manasseh could not take at first (Joshua 17:11; Judges 1:27). By Solomon's time they were part of the kingdom and formed one rich district across the great valley.

decisions.choice: which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel: a description of the Beth-shean area
decisions.reason: The clause tells where the district of Beth-shean lay: by Zarethan, in the Jordan valley, and lower than the town of Jezreel on the hills to the west. The next phrase gives its limits, south to Abel-meholah and beyond Jokmeam.

decisions.choice: Baana son of Ahilud: perhaps a brother of the recorder
decisions.reason: Jehoshaphat the recorder was also a son of Ahilud (verse 3). They may be brothers, but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: two sentences, with "that area"
decisions.reason: Readable divides the long description and repeats the subject, "that area", so the reader can follow where the district lay.

decisions.choice: "Meguido", "Bet-sán", "Jezreel"
decisions.reason: Megiddo and Jezreel follow the Kings terms note; Beth-shean keeps "Bet-sán", the form of the Spanish of 1 Samuel 31 and 2 Samuel 21; the other towns take their usual Spanish forms.

source.text: בֶּן־גֶּ֖בֶר בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד ל֡וֹ חַוֺּת֩ יָאִ֨יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּגִּלְעָ֗ד ל֚וֹ חֶ֤בֶל אַרְגֹּב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּבָּשָׁ֔ן שִׁשִּׁים֙ עָרִ֣ים גְּדֹל֔וֹת חוֹמָ֖ה וּבְרִ֥יחַ נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead; to him [were the] villages of Jair son of Manasseh which [are] in Gilead; to him [was the] region of Argob which [is] in Bashan, sixty cities great, wall and bar[s] of bronze.

en.L: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead; his [were] the villages of Jair son of Manasseh, which [are] in Gilead; his [was] the region of Argob, which [is] in Bashan, sixty great cities [with] wall[s] and bronze bar[s];
en.B: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead. The villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead were his, and so was the region of Argob in Bashan: sixty large cities with walls and bronze bars;
en.R: Ben-geber was over Ramoth-gilead. His district included the villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead and the region of Argob in Bashan. There were sixty large cities there, with walls and with gates locked by bronze bars.

es.L: Ben-geber, en Ramot de Galaad; suyas [eran] las aldeas de Jair hijo de Manasés, que [están] en Galaad; suya [era] la región de Argob, que [está] en Basán, sesenta ciudades grandes [con] muros y cerrojos de bronce;
es.B: Ben-geber, en Ramot de Galaad. Eran suyas las aldeas de Jair hijo de Manasés en Galaad, y también la región de Argob en Basán: sesenta ciudades grandes con murallas y cerrojos de bronce;
es.R: Ben-geber estaba a cargo de Ramot de Galaad. Su distrito incluía las aldeas de Jair hijo de Manasés en Galaad, y la región de Argob en Basán. Allí había sesenta ciudades grandes con murallas, y con puertas cerradas con barras de bronce.

fr.L: Ben-Guéber, à Ramoth de Galaad ; à lui [étaient] les villages de Yaïr fils de Manassé, qui [sont] en Galaad ; à lui [était] la région d’Argob, qui [est] en Bashân, soixante grandes villes [avec] muraille et verrous de bronze ;
fr.B: Ben-Guéber, à Ramoth de Galaad. Les villages de Yaïr fils de Manassé, en Galaad, étaient à lui, ainsi que la région d’Argob en Bashân : soixante grandes villes avec des murailles et des verrous de bronze ;
fr.R: Ben-Guéber était responsable de Ramoth de Galaad. Son district comprenait les villages de Yaïr, fils de Manassé, en Galaad, et la région d’Argob en Bashân. Il y avait là soixante grandes villes, avec des murailles et des portes fermées par des barres de bronze.

sw.L: Ben-geberi, katika Ramoth-gileadi; vijiji vya Yairi mwana wa Manase, [vilivyo] katika Gileadi, [vilikuwa] vyake; eneo la Argobu, [lililo] katika Bashani, [lilikuwa] lake, miji mikubwa sitini [yenye] kuta na makomeo ya shaba;
sw.B: Ben-geberi, katika Ramoth-gileadi. Vijiji vya Yairi mwana wa Manase katika Gileadi vilikuwa chini yake, pamoja na eneo la Argobu katika Bashani: miji mikubwa sitini yenye kuta na makomeo ya shaba;
sw.R: Ben-geberi alikuwa juu ya Ramoth-gileadi. Wilaya yake ilikuwa na vijiji vya Yairi mwana wa Manase katika Gileadi, na eneo la Argobu katika Bashani. Huko kulikuwa na miji mikubwa sitini yenye kuta, na malango yaliyofungwa kwa makomeo ya shaba.

vi.L: Bên-Ghê-be, tại Ra-mốt Ga-la-át; các làng của Giai-rơ con trai Ma-na-se ở Ga-la-át [thuộc về] ông; miền Ạt-gốp ở Ba-san [thuộc về] ông, sáu mươi thành lớn [có] tường và then cửa bằng đồng;
vi.B: Bên-Ghê-be, tại Ra-mốt Ga-la-át. Các làng của Giai-rơ con trai Ma-na-se ở Ga-la-át thuộc quyền ông, cùng miền Ạt-gốp ở Ba-san: sáu mươi thành lớn có tường và then cửa bằng đồng;
vi.R: Bên-Ghê-be cai trị Ra-mốt Ga-la-át. Vùng của ông gồm các làng của Giai-rơ con trai Ma-na-se ở Ga-la-át, và miền Ạt-gốp ở Ba-san. Ở đó có sáu mươi thành lớn, có tường bao quanh và cổng cài then bằng đồng.

ko.L: 길르앗 라못에는 벤게벨, 그에게 길르앗에 있는 므낫세의 아들 야일의 마을들이 [속했고], 그에게 바산에 있는 아르곱 지역, 곧 성벽과 놋 빗장을 [갖춘] 큰 성읍 육십 개가 [속했다].
ko.B: 길르앗 라못에는 벤게벨, 길르앗에 있는 므낫세의 아들 야일의 마을들과 바산에 있는 아르곱 지역도 그의 관할이었는데, 그곳에는 성벽과 놋 빗장을 갖춘 큰 성읍이 육십 개 있었다.
ko.R: 벤게벨은 길르앗 라못을 맡았다. 그가 맡은 지역에는 길르앗에 있는 므낫세의 아들 야일의 마을들과 바산에 있는 아르곱 지역이 들어 있었다. 그곳에는 큰 성읍이 육십 개 있었는데, 성벽이 둘러 있고 성문은 놋 빗장으로 잠겨 있었다.

pt.L: Ben-Geber, em Ramote-Gileade; dele [eram] as aldeias de Jair, filho de Manassés, que [estão] em Gileade; dele [era] a região de Argobe, que [está] em Basã, sessenta cidades grandes [com] muro[s] e trancas de bronze;
pt.B: Ben-Geber, em Ramote-Gileade. As aldeias de Jair, filho de Manassés, em Gileade, eram dele, e também a região de Argobe, em Basã: sessenta cidades grandes, com muralhas e trancas de bronze;
pt.R: Ben-Geber governava Ramote-Gileade. O seu distrito incluía as aldeias de Jair, filho de Manassés, em Gileade, e a região de Argobe, em Basã. Ali havia sessenta cidades grandes, com muralhas e com portões fechados por trancas de bronze.

decisions.choice: the villages of Jair and the sixty cities of Argob: the lands taken under Moses
decisions.reason: Jair son of Manasseh took the region of Argob and named its villages after himself (Numbers 32:41; Deuteronomy 3:14). Deuteronomy 3:4-5 describes the sixty fortified cities of Argob with high walls, gates and bars.

decisions.choice: wall and bars of bronze: fortified towns
decisions.reason: The bars were the beams that held the city gates shut. Bronze made them harder to break or burn.

decisions.choice: Ramoth-gilead: a fortress town east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: It was a city of refuge (Joshua 20:8) and later a battleground between Israel and Aram (22:3). Ben-geber is a "son of" name, as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: bronze bars (Balanced); gates locked by bronze bars (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the bars were for, as the note explains.

decisions.choice: Ramoth de Galaad; Yaïr; Bashân
decisions.reason: French forms kept for Kings: Ramoth de Galaad, as Yabesh de Galaad in Samuel.

decisions.choice: "놋" for bronze
decisions.reason: As the Kings and Chronicles terms note ("놋 바다; 놋"), one word for bronze through the temple chapters.

decisions.choice: Ramote-Gileade
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 22:3-29): the town is written as one name with a hyphen, as the English writes it and as Kings uses it again and again; Deuteronomy 4:43 and Joshua 20:8 in Portuguese say "Ramote, em Gileade", the same place. "Argobe" as Deuteronomy 3:4, 14 in Portuguese, and "as aldeias de Jair" as Deuteronomy 3:14 (Readable) explains the name Havote-Jair.

decisions.choice: the land of Sihon and Og: the kingdoms east of the Jordan taken under Moses
decisions.reason: Israel defeated Sihon and Og and gave their land to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh (Numbers 21:21-35; Deuteronomy 3:1-17). Ben-geber's district (verse 13) lay in Gilead too, so these two districts shared the land east of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: one governor who was in the land: meaning unclear
alternatives: he was the only governor in that land
and one governor over the land of Judah
decisions.reason: The words may mean that Geber was the only governor over this wide region, or that there was one more governor, over "the land", perhaps Judah, which the list does not otherwise name. The ancient Greek translation has "in the land of Judah" here. The Hebrew can bear both readings, and all levels keep it open.

decisions.choice: Long before, this land had belonged to
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the names of Sihon and Og recall who once ruled the land.

decisions.choice: um governador
decisions.reason: The words are unclear (m2): Geber may have been the only governor of this wide region, or there may have been one more governor, over the land of Judah. Portuguese "um governador" keeps both readings open, as the English does; "um só" or "mais um" would each choose one.

en.B: Judah and Israel were as many as the sand by the sea; they ate and drank and were glad.
en.R: The people of Judah and Israel were as many as the grains of sand on the seashore. They had plenty to eat and drink, and they were happy.

es.L: Judá e Israel [eran] muchos, como la arena que [está] junto al mar en multitud, comiendo y bebiendo y alegrándose.

fr.L: Juda et Israël [étaient] nombreux comme le sable qui [est] au bord de la mer en multitude, mangeant, et buvant, et se réjouissant.
fr.B: Juda et Israël étaient aussi nombreux que le sable au bord de la mer ; ils mangeaient, buvaient et se réjouissaient.
fr.R: Les gens de Juda et d’Israël étaient aussi nombreux que les grains de sable au bord de la mer. Ils avaient de quoi manger et boire en abondance, et ils étaient heureux.

sw.L: Yuda na Israeli [walikuwa] wengi, kama mchanga ulio kando ya bahari kwa wingi, wakila na kunywa na kufurahi.

sw.R: Watu wa Yuda na Israeli walikuwa wengi kama chembe za mchanga ufuoni mwa bahari. Walikuwa na chakula na kinywaji kingi, nao walikuwa na furaha.

ko.L: 유다와 이스라엘은 바닷가의 모래처럼 수가 많았고, 먹고 마시며 즐거워했다.
ko.B: 유다와 이스라엘 사람들은 바닷가의 모래처럼 많았으며, 먹고 마시며 즐겁게 지냈다.
ko.R: 유다와 이스라엘 백성은 바닷가의 모래알처럼 많았다. 그들은 먹을 것과 마실 것이 넉넉했고 행복하게 살았다.

pt.L: Judá e Israel [eram] numerosos como a areia que [está] junto ao mar em multidão, comendo, e bebendo, e se alegrando.
pt.B: Judá e Israel eram tão numerosos como a areia à beira-mar; comiam, bebiam e se alegravam.
pt.R: O povo de Judá e de Israel era tão numeroso como os grãos de areia da praia. Eles tinham comida e bebida com fartura e viviam felizes.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text ends chapter 4 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 4 ends at this verse, and the next fourteen verses (Solomon's wide rule, his daily provisions and his wisdom) begin chapter 5 as 5:1-14. Many Bibles number them 4:21-34, and so number the rest of chapter 5 (5:15-32 here) 5:1-18. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: as many as the sand by the sea: God's promise to Abraham kept
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham to make his offspring like the sand on the seashore (Genesis 22:17; see also 32:13). The writer shows that promise fulfilled in Solomon's day.

decisions.choice: eating and drinking and rejoicing: peace and plenty
decisions.reason: The three words picture a people with enough food, at peace and glad, under a king who ruled them well. "Judah and Israel" names the south and the north together, still one kingdom.
